summary: 1933 Payette NF fire tower moved in 2000 to the Central Idaho Historical Museum in McCall, where its cab and 10 feet of tower are on display.

facts.design: Prefabricated Aermotor tower, 72 ft, with a log cabin residence built alongside (1933)
facts.status_note: Only the cab and 10 feet of the original 72-foot tower are on display at the museum.

access.note: Shown on the grounds of the Central Idaho Historical Museum, 1001 State St., McCall. The museum is open June through August, Wednesday to Saturday.

notes_for_editor: Sources agree on the 1933 build, the 1994 cabin removal and the 2000 move to the museum. They disagree on staffing: NHLR says staffed into the 1970s; the marker says staffed 1934-1970; Idaho Fire Lookouts says no longer staffed in the 1970s. The story reports all three. Elevation: NHLR gives 5,021 ft for the museum coordinates; Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 6,280 ft, which may be the original site. Name variants: 'Sloans Creek Point' (record and FFLA index), 'Sloans Point' (NHLR), 'Sloan's Point' (marker). A separate record us-id-sloans-creek-point exists (FFLA 'Standing' at 44.74488, -115.92730); it may be the original site, so the two may need linking or review. Not used: search snippets (not fetchable) from a Waymarking/HMdb marker text say Ed Allen and his son dismantled the tower in 2000 and Richard Holm Jr. and volunteers restored it in 2006. The Waymarking body is not cached (JS-rendered) and the HMdb inscription is truncated, so these lines cannot be quoted; a human should check them. The 2006 date conflicts with NHLR's 2000 reconstruction account. Access and hours come from AllTrips, a travel site; the museum's own site was not checked and hours may have changed. No photos added; the NHLR photo of the interpretive panel is credited to waymarking.com with unknown licence.
